data.content_ref: inline:The proposed reduction of the 'reliability paradox' to the tension between raising the floor and lowering the ceiling lacks the causal mechanism the problem standard requires. The target asserts a reductive relation but never identifies the actual causal variable that links floor-ceiling tension to fatigue-induced noise — it merely asserts that attempting to capture more signal increases noise through cognitive load. Without specifying the mechanism by which raising the floor mechanically produces fatigue and how that fatigue degrades reliability, the claimed reduction is an ungrounded label assignment, not a substantive reduction.
